decisions.title: Marketing is a pure passthrough — forward three fields, touch no storage
decisions.chose: Forward couchdrop_shared_link_url + practice_email + email_type straight to HubSpot.
decisions.rejected: Have marketing read S3 / call Couchdrop / hold Couchdrop credentials to build the link itself
decisions.why: Scoping marketing to a passthrough keeps blast radius tiny: no S3, no Couchdrop, no Couchdrop credentials. The payload builder is the whole of its data handling.

provenanceTrail.reason: plan approved (ClaudePlanApproved) — passthrough scope, flag gate, idempotency, and payload-typing approach signed off

decisions.title: Gate the send behind a flag that ships off, keyed on practice with no PHI
decisions.chose: Evaluate marketing-practice-report-send-enabled with context { kind: "practice", key: practice_sf_account_id }, fallback false.
decisions.rejected: Ship the send path live, or key the flag on the recipient / patient
decisions.why: Flag ships off and is flipped on deliberately after deploy, so the new path changes nothing until intended, and can be withdrawn during a HubSpot incident with no redeploy. Context carries only the SF account id — no PHI to LaunchDarkly. Fails closed.

decisions.title: Claim an idempotency slot so redelivery never double-sends
decisions.chose: Claim (practice_id, report_type, batch_period) before sending; a lost claim refuses the send.
decisions.rejected: Send on every delivery, or check-then-insert (racy under concurrent partitions)
decisions.why: Kafka is at-least-once and the consumer runs four partitions concurrently, so the same report can arrive twice. An atomic INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING turns duplicate delivery into a no-op instead of a duplicate email.

decisions.title: Give the practice-report send its own payload type — don't widen the union
decisions.chose: Add HubSpotPracticeReportWebhookPayload as a separate type, accepted by sendHubSpotWebhook via a union at the parameter.
decisions.rejected: Add the practice-report case as a member of the existing HubSpotWebhookPayload union
decisions.why: On trying to widen the union, tsc broke narrowing in buildPartnerReferralWebhookPayload — that union is closed over the partner-referral EmailType and the builder relies on the closure. A separate type carries no per-patient enrichment and leaves every consumer that narrows on the old union untouched.

provenanceTrail.reason: planned to reuse the union (seq 4); widening it broke narrowing in buildPartnerReferralWebhookPayload, so switched to a standalone type
diff-critic confirmed the standalone type leaves the partner-referral union's narrowing intact; anchor hubspot-webhook-client.ts:33-45 resolves at HEAD

history.chose: Add the practice-report case as a member of HubSpotWebhookPayload so sendHubSpotWebhook takes it unchanged.
history.why: Reuse the union the partner-referral path already flows through — one type, one send function, less to add.

decisions.title: Decompose the handler into gate → claim → send
decisions.chose: Split practiceReportGenerated into three guard-clause steps: is-send-enabled, claim-slot, send-claimed.
decisions.rejected: One method that flag-checks, claims, composes, POSTs, and releases inline
decisions.why: Each step is a guard that returns early, so the happy path reads top to bottom and each precondition is checkable in isolation. Mirrors the established PartnerReferralSubscription flow, so a reviewer who knows that precedent knows this shape.

tests.name: makes no HubSpot request when the flag is off
never claims a slot when the flag is off

decisions.title: Release the slot on send failure so a later flip re-drives cleanly
decisions.chose: Track a sent flag; in finally, release the claim if the send did not succeed, then rethrow.
decisions.rejected: Leave the slot claimed on failure (permanent), or release unconditionally
decisions.why: A claimed-but-unsent slot would permanently block that report — a HubSpot outage would swallow it forever. Releasing only on failure lets a retry or later flag flip re-drive; releasing unconditionally would defeat the idempotency guard on the success path. Rethrowing preserves at-least-once retry.

decisions.title: Leave the producer's report_type field on the wire schema
decisions.chose: Keep PracticeReportEntity.report_type in event-schemas.ts even though the handler claims on email_type.
decisions.why: It is the producer's wire contract; removing it would be a schema/contract change on a shared topic, out of scope for this send-path PR.

provenanceTrail.reason: review flagged report_type as unused; declined — it's the producer's contract, not ours to drop here

decisions.title: Keep the catch-block log identical to the partner-referral precedent
decisions.chose: Log event.uuid / event.trace_id as raw Public<> wrappers in the generated-handler catch, matching the shipped PartnerReferralCreatedEventHandler byte-for-byte.
decisions.rejected: Unwrap .value() in the log line here
decisions.why: The handler is a deliberate byte-for-byte copy of the shipped precedent; diverging the log format in this PR would fork the two handlers for no behavioural gain.

provenanceTrail.reason: review noted the wrappers aren't unwrapped; declined — matching the precedent copy is the point
